why: Actor kind. Both sides reject packing (ADR 0103 SendableRef): the compile-time checker's kind-based fallback (tier_of_known, ClassKind::Actor arm) and the runtime walk (field_tier/1, kind =:= actor arm) agree.

Object kind declaring handleScope: #process. Both sides reject packing (ADR 0103 HandleScoped): the compile-time checker's kind-based fallback (tier_of_known, ClassKind::Object arm with a resolved handle_scope) and the runtime walk (field_tier/1, kind =:= object with a handle_scope key present) agree.

Value kind, no hazardous fields. Both sides treat this as packable, under each side's own vocabulary for 'packable': Rust's tier_of_known composes the Value's fields eagerly and returns a single terminal Tier::Sendable, while the runtime field_tier/1 returns value_nested — an instruction to pack/1's caller to recurse into the instance's own fields, not a terminal answer itself. Both mean 'not rejected here.'

DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE (BT-3542): an Object subclass declaring neither handleScope: nor any other classification. The compile-time checker is silent about it (Tier::Unknown, ADR 0100 advisory-only — nothing to warn about, since it has no compile-time opinion). The runtime walk conservatively ALLOWS it through pack/1 as an opaque, unversioned term (passthrough) since it carries no known hazard. This is an intentional asymmetry, not a bug: pack/1 must make a binary allow/reject decision at runtime, while the compile-time checker is free to abstain. See beamtalk_shape_migration.erl's field_tier/1 doc and beamtalk_shape_migration_tests.erl's sendability tier conformance test.
